# Preparation Meetings {#sec-preparation .unnumbered}

For the day to run smoothly, **it is essential that all attendees take part in both preparation meetings.** They let teams meet in advance, agree their problem statement and get the technical workspace working before arriving in Newcastle.

| Meeting | Date and time | Purpose |
|------------------|------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **1. Team meeting** | **Monday 30 November** · 30-minute slot per team, 11:00–13:00 | Meet your team and receive your problem statement |
| **2. EODH workspace introduction** | **Wednesday 2 December** · 11:00–12:00 | Introduction to the EODH technical workspace |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Team meeting — Monday 30 November {.unnumbered}

**Format:** online, on Microsoft Teams. Each team has its own meeting link, sent by **Brigid Bell** ([brigid.bell\@liverpool.ac.uk](mailto:brigid.bell@liverpool.ac.uk)). If you haven't received yours, or need to change slot, please get in touch with Brigid.

| Time | Team | Mentor |
|------|------|--------|
| 11:00–11:30 | Surface Tension | Munazza Usmani |
| 11:30–12:00 | Green Buffer | Ron Mahabir |
| 12:00–12:30 | Unequal Degrees | Elisabetta Pietrostefani |
| 12:30–13:00 | Degrees Apart | Vitaly Kryukov |

In this session you will:

-   Meet the other members of your team
-   Receive your team's **problem statement** from our policy partners
-   Discuss what decision the problem statement supports and who would use the output
-   Agree roles for the day (e.g. data lead, policy lead, presenter)

::: callout-note
**Can't attend?**\
If you can't make your team's slot, you can contribute **by email** instead. Let Brigid know in advance and we'll share the problem statement and ask for your input on scope and roles.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. EODH workspace introduction — Wednesday 2 December, 11:00–12:00 {.unnumbered}

:::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Online, on Microsoft Teams · Wednesday 2 December, 11:00–12:00**

[Join the meeting on Microsoft Teams](https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/3353412826008209?p=yVU7TqG3ISda1yISH9){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg role="button" target="_blank"}
::::

The Earth Observation Data Hub (EODH) and Imago teams will introduce the technical workspace you'll use on the day. We'll take questions as we go.

| Time | Session | Led by |
|------|---------|--------|
| 10 min | **Introduction to EODH:** what the Hub is for, what it can do, and why it is useful for accessing and analysing Earth observation data | EODH |
| 10 min | **Platform overview and demo:** navigating the platform; workspaces, computing environments and storage; finding other datasets such as Landsat and Sentinel-2; managing files, saving work and exporting outputs; limitations and good practice | EODH |
| 25 min | **Hackathon workspaces, datasets and notebooks:** opening your team workspace and launching Jupyter; finding the preloaded datasets and materials; walking through the Python notebooks; running example code to load, explore, analyse and visualise the data | Imago |
| 5 min | **Next steps:** what to do before the hackathon, documentation, resources and where to get technical support | Imago |

::: callout-tip
**Before 2 December**\
Create your EODH account (with a GitHub, Google or Microsoft login) and send us the email address you used, following **Steps 1–2 of [Getting Started with EODH](eodh-start.qmd)**. If you have time, have a look at the [starter notebooks and data](https://github.com/Imago-SDRUK/Imago-EODH-Hack-2026/tree/main/tutorial) on GitHub (see [Resources](resources.qmd#hackathon-notebooks-and-data)).
:::

Policy participants are very welcome at this session too — seeing what the workspace can do will help when shaping your team's question — but it is most important for technical participants.
